title: Slow Kernel Detection and Hotfix Playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

This playbook describes detection, automated containment, and manual hotfix procedures for incidents where a GPU kernel (or small set of kernels) regress in latency or CPU/GPU time and produce sustained throughput degradation. It focuses on actionable detection signals, escalation thresholds, immediate mitigations to protect SLAs, and validated release steps for kernel hotfixes.

Scope

- Applies to production inference runtime kernels (attention, fused-matmul, kv-cache ops, rotary/rope ops) across hosted and dedicated clusters.
- Does NOT cover hardware faults (power/thermal fails) or driver-level crashes — those are handled by infrastructure runbooks.

Ownership and contacts

- Incident owner: eng-serving-runtime oncall (primary).
- Kernel lead: @Maya Chen (runtime-kernels).
- Escalation: runtime-arch-sre@redwood.internal.

When to use this playbook

Use this playbook when:
1) Kernel latency spike or variance is correlated with increased end-to-end p95/p99 serving latency for >5 minutes.
2) Throughput drop or request queuing increases by >30% while GPU utilization is not saturated.
3) Automated regression detection (see Alerting rules) fires.

Detection signals and telemetry

Primary metrics to monitor (examples):
- kernel.exec_time_ms (histogram per kernel): sudden shift in median or tail.
- kernel.cpu_time_ms and kernel.gpu_time_ms: divergence indicates scheduling/serialization issues.
- runtime.request_queue_depth: sustained increase suggests backpressure.
- gpu_utilization_pct: if <85% while queue depth grows => kernel stalls/serialization.
- kernel.retry_count / kernel_ejection_count: raised ejection counts.

Suggested alert rules (promQL-like pseudocode):

- name: KernelTailLatencyExceeded
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(kernel_exec_time_ms_bucket[2m])) by (le,kernel)) > 12
  for: 4m

- name: KernelVarianceSpike
  expr: (quantile_over_time(0.95, kernel_exec_time_ms[10m]) / quantile_over_time(0.5, kernel_exec_time_ms[10m])) > 4
  for: 3m

- name: QueueGrowthWithLowUtil
  expr: (increase(runtime_request_queue_depth[5m]) > 30) and (avg_over_time(gpu_utilization_pct[5m]) < 85)
  for: 5m

Investigation timeline (first 30 minutes)

1) Triage (0–5m):
   - Acknowledge alert in PagerDuty and tag with incident channel.
   - Attach the alert graph and note the affected model(s)/cluster(s).

2) Quick checks (5–12m):
   - Confirm whether regression is per-kernel or broad: query kernel.exec_time_ms grouped by kernel_name and host.
   - Check recent releases or kernel rollouts in the last 60 minutes.
   - Inspect kernel ejection logs and driver warnings.

3) Decide containment (12–20m):
   - If kernel impact is limited to a subset of workers, use targeted quarantine (see Automated mitigations).
   - If impact is global or affects control-plane operations, follow full degradation playbook and notify product & CS.

Automated mitigations (safe by default)

We prefer automated, reversible actions to avoid manual intervention during noisy transient spikes. Typical automated mitigations:

- Kernel quarantine: mark kernel variant as degraded and route traffic to next-compatible variant (e.g., fallback quantized kernel or older kernel build).
- Per-host kernel disable: use runtime-agent to toggle kernel blacklist on affected hosts.
- Graceful request shed: temporarily reduce concurrency for affected hosts and redirect to healthy pools.

Automation pseudocode (internal operator):

# Example internal CLI commands
redwood-runtimectl quarantine-kernel --kernel-name fused_attn_v2 --reason "p95 regression 2026-02-28" --scope hosts=pool-3b
redwood-runtimectl set-concurrency --host host-12 --max-concurrency 2

Containment decision matrix (summary):
| Impact pattern | Immediate action | Rationale |
|---|---:|---|
| Single-host / single-kernel | Kernel quarantine + local restart | Limits blast radius |
| Multi-host same kernel | Route to fallback variant + scale healthy pool | Prevents large SLA violations |
| Global performance regression | Activate degradation SLOs and roll back recent kernel rollout | Protect customer-facing SLAs |

Manual hotfix procedure (if automation insufficient)

1) Create incident branch and patch:
   - Branch from release-tag: git checkout -b hotfix/kernel-<id>-<date> release/<tag>
   - Add guard-logging (timestamps + kernel id) and revert recent non-essential optimizations if needed.

2) Build and smoke test in staging:
   - Build: make -C runtime kernels && ./tools/build-kernel --name hotfix-kernel --ccache
   - Unit smoke: ./tools/smoke-runner --kernel hotfix-kernel --profile micro-latency
   - Perf microbench: ./bench/kernel-bench --kernel hotfix-kernel --seq-lens 8,64,512 --shots 200

3) Canaried rollout (targeted pattern):
   - Canary to 2–3 hosts with mirrored traffic for 10m.
   - Metrics to watch during canary: p50/p95 kernel.exec_time_ms, request_queue_depth, gpu_utilization, error_rate.
   - Canary acceptance criteria: no >5% regression vs baseline on p50 and <3% change in p95.

4) Gradual ramp: 20% -> 50% -> 100% or by host pools depending on topology. Evaluate at each step for 10–15 minutes.

Rollback criteria and steps

Rollback if any of the following occurs during canary or ramp:
- p95 increases by >10% relative to the pre-incident baseline.
- request queue depth increases by >2x.
- error rate (5xx) increases above SLO thresholds.

Rollback steps:
1) Immediately set routing to previous kernel variant using runtime controller.
2) Drain canary hosts and reboot agent if necessary: systemctl restart runtime-agent on canary hosts.
3) Mark hotfix branch for postmortem and revert patch in mainline if necessary.

Verification checklist after rollback/hotfix

- Verify kernel.exec_time_ms histograms have returned to baseline over 30 minutes.
- Validate no increase in request_retries or request_timeouts.
- Confirm logs show no new driver warnings.
- Close incident with updates to relevant oncall and product teams.

Post-incident follow-up

- Owner prepares postmortem within 72 hours: root cause, timeline, mitigations, action items.
- If kernel regression was caused by a code change, add mandatory microbench in CI for the offending kernel with 95th percentile assertions.
- Schedule a retro with kernel authors and SRE to adjust thresholds or automation if false positives/negatives caused disruption.

Testing and benchmark additions

When a kernel shows instability add these tests to the CI pipeline:
- Deterministic microbenchmark for sequence lengths: 8, 32, 128, 512 (200 iterations each).
- Telemetry spike test: inject synthetic jitter and assert no >2x increase in hardware stall markers.
- Multi-host soak test: run 60-minute concurrent-run against a mirrored traffic profile.

Quick reference commands

- Query per-kernel tail latency (internal monitoring):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $MONITOR_TOKEN" "https://monitoring.internal/api/query?q=kernel_exec_time_ms%7Bcluster%3D%5C\"prod%5C\"%7D"

- Quarantine kernel: redwood-runtimectl quarantine-kernel --kernel-name <kernel> --scope hosts=<pool>
- Re-enable kernel: redwood-runtimectl unquarantine-kernel --kernel-name <kernel>
- Canary rollout: redwood-runtimectl deploy-kernel --image hotfix-kernel:canary --hosts host-12,host-13

Appendix: recommended thresholds (editable)

| Setting | Default value | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| p95_kernel_latency_alert_ms | 12 | Trigger for KernelTailLatencyExceeded rule |
| kernel_variance_ratio_alert | 4 | Ratio of p95/p50 over 10m window |
| queue_growth_pct_alert | 30 | Percent growth over 5 minutes |
| canary_observe_window | 10m | Observation window for canary acceptance |
